**7B.1 Research Note**
Overall: mostly no. The 2024 record shows repeated self-serving, misleading, or contradicted statements on the election, protests, and foreign interference claims. I found only weak counterevidence: a few statements that were later framed as corrections or accountability, but not a durable pattern of truth-telling.

**Negative evidence**
- **Bangladesh PM Hasina blames opposition for violence, curfew to remain** | Reuters | July 22, 2024 | [source](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladesh-pm-hasina-blames-opposition-for-violence-curfew-to-remain-3528153) | Hasina blamed opposition parties for the violence and said the curfew was imposed to protect lives and property. Later reporting showed the state response was far deadlier and more coercive than this framing suggested, so this is strong evidence of self-justifying misrepresentation to the public. | `7B.1` `1B.8` `
I’ve got the core picture, but I’m doing one last bounded pass for direct instances where her claims were contradicted or later walked back, since those are the strongest truthfulness signals.

item.text:
**7B.1 Research Note**
Overall: mostly no. I found repeated cases where Hasina’s public line was self-serving or contradicted by later reporting, especially on the election and the July crackdown. The only counterevidence I found was weak and mostly post-hoc.

**Weak counterevidence**
- **US says it had no role in ousting of Bangladesh PM Hasina** | Reuters via The Straits Times | August 13, 2024 | [source](https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/us-says-it-had-no-role-in-ousting-of-bangladeshs-hasina) | The White House publicly denied U.S. involvement, and the report says Hasina’s son said she never made the alleged Saint Martin’s Island statement. This is weak counterevidence only: it shows a disputed attribution, not a strong pattern of truthfulness. | `7B.1` `1B.8`
- **Former Bangladesh PM Hasina demands probe into July killings and vandalism** | Reuters | August 13, 2024 | [source](https://theprint.in/world/former-bangladesh-pm-hasina-demands-probe-into-july-killings-and-vandalism/2222256/) | After fleeing, Hasina called for an investigation into the killings and vandalism. This is the closest accountability signal I found, but it is post-hoc and does not show that she was candid while in power. | `7B.1` `1B.8`

**Negative evidence**
- **Bangladesh PM Hasina blames opposition for violence, curfew to remain** | Reuters | July 22, 2024 | [source](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladesh-pm-hasina-blames-opposition-for-violence-curfew-to-remain-3528153) | Hasina publicly blamed political opponents for deadly violence and kept the curfew in place. That reads as self-justifying blame-shifting rather than truthful explanation. | `7B.1` `1B.8`
- **Bangladesh army enforces curfew as student-led protests spiral** | Reuters | July 20, 2024 | [source](https://theprint.in/world/bangladesh-army-enforces-curfew-as-student-led-protests-spiral/2182818/) | The government imposed a curfew, internet/text shutdowns, and army deployment. Later UN and HRW reporting strongly undercut the implied necessity and proportionality of that narrative. | `7B.1` `1B.8`
- **Bangladesh’s elections extending Hasina’s rule were not credible** | Associated Press | January 8, 2024 | [source](https://ny1.com/nyc/all-boroughs/ap-top-news/2024/01/09/the-us-and-uk-say-bangladeshs-elections-extending-hasinas-rule-were-not-credible) | AP reported that key foreign partners said the election was not credible amid violence and arrests. This undercuts any truthful public portrayal of the vote as a fair contest. | `7B.1` `1B.5` `1B.8`
- **Bangladesh crackdown leaves more than 170 dead** | UN OHCHR | July 26, 2024 | [source](https://bangladesh.un.org/en/275065-bangladesh-t%C3%BCrk-decries-government-crackdown-urges-respect-international-human-rights) | The UN said more than 170 people were killed, some injured people were denied medical care, and internet shutdowns increased impunity. That sharply contradicts any candid claim that the government response was protective or restrained. | `7B.1` `6B.6` `1B.8`

**Synthesis**
- The strongest negative pattern is not one isolated falsehood but repeated self-serving framing under pressure: election legitimacy, protest violence, curfew necessity, and foreign-interference narratives.
- I did not find strong affirmative evidence that Hasina habitually corrected herself or told uncomfortable truths when deception would have protected her position.
- The best counterevidence is thin: one post-hoc call for investigation and a denial that a quoted U.S.-plot accusation was actually hers.

**Search gap**
- I did not find direct, well-sourced instances of Hasina telling the truth in situations where lying would have clearly protected her power or reputation.
- I also did not find a strong court-facing truthfulness record in 2024. Most evidence available is public statements, crisis framing, and later contradictions rather than formal sworn testimony.
